title.zh: 卷268 列傳五十五 米思翰 顾八代 玛尔汉 田六善 杜臻 萨穆哈
title.en: Volume 268 Biographies 55: Mi Sihan, Gu Badai, Ma Er Han, Tian Liushan, Du Zhen, Sa Mu Ha
title.raw: 卷268 列傳五十五 米思翰 顾八代 玛尔汉 田六善 杜臻 萨穆哈

sentences.zh: 列傳五十五

translations.literal: Biographies 55
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 55

sentences.zh: 米思翰子李榮保顧八代瑪爾漢田六善杜臻薩穆哈

translations.literal: Mi Sihan, Li Rongbao, Gu Badai, Ma Erhan, Tian Liushan, Du Zhen, Sa Muha
translations.idiomatic: Mi Sihan, Li Rongbao, Gu Badai, Ma Erhan, Tian Liushan, Du Zhen, and Sa Muha

sentences.zh: 米思翰，富察氏，滿洲鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: Mi Sihan, of the Fuca clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Sihan, of the Fuca clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 先世居沙濟。

translations.literal: His ancestors had lived at Shaji.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long resided at Shaji.

sentences.zh: 曾祖旺吉努，當太祖時，率族來歸，授牛錄額真。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Wangjinu, in the time of the Taizu, led the clan to submit and was appointed niru commander.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Wangjinu submitted with the clan during the Taizu's reign and was appointed niru commander.

sentences.zh: 父哈什屯，事太宗，以侍衛襲管牛錄。

translations.literal: His father Hashun served the Taizong; as a bodyguard he inherited management of the niru.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hashun served the Taizong and, as an imperial guardsman, inherited command of the family niru.

sentences.zh: 擢禮部參政，改副理事官。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Ministry of Rites and then transferred to Associate Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Commissioner in the Ministry of Rites and was later made Associate Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 討瓦爾喀，招明總兵沈志祥。

translations.literal: Campaigning against Warka, he induced the Ming regional commander Shen Zhixiang to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign against Warka he won over the Ming regional commander Shen Zhixiang.

sentences.zh: 從攻錦州，明總兵曹變蛟夜襲御營，先眾扞禦，被創，力戰卻之。

translations.literal: He followed the attack on Jinzhou; the Ming regional commander Cao Bianjiao raided the imperial camp by night—he was first among the troops to resist, was wounded, and fought fiercely to drive the enemy back.
translations.idiomatic: At the siege of Jinzhou, when the Ming commander Cao Bianjiao struck the imperial camp by night, Hashun was first to meet the assault. Though wounded, he fought hard and repulsed the attack.

sentences.zh: 順治初，授內大臣、議政大臣，世職屢進一等阿達哈哈番兼拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: Early in Shunzhi he was appointed Grand Minister of the Imperial Household and Grand Councilor; his hereditary rank was repeatedly advanced to first-class adahahafan with tashalahafan attached.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shunzhi reign he became a Grand Minister of the Imperial Household and a Grand Councilor, and his hereditary rank was raised repeatedly until he held first-class adahahafan with an additional tashalahafan.

sentences.zh: 睿親王多爾袞攝政，諸大臣鞏阿岱等並附之，哈什屯獨持正，忤睿親王，降世職拜他喇布勒哈番。

translations.literal: When Prince Regent Dorgon held power, ministers such as Gongadai all sided with him; Hashun alone held to what was right, offended the Prince Regent, and had his hereditary rank reduced to batalabulehafan.
translations.idiomatic: While Prince Regent Dorgon governed, ministers including Gongadai rallied to him, but Hashun alone stood firm. He offended the prince regent and was demoted to batalabulehafan.

sentences.zh: 肅親王豪格以非罪死，鞏阿岱等議殺其子富綬，哈什屯與巴哈力持，事乃已。

translations.literal: Prince Su Haoge died on a false charge; Gongadai and others proposed killing his son Fushou—Hashun and Bahali held firm against it, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Su Haoge was put to death on trumped-up charges, Gongadai and others urged that his son Fushou be killed as well. Hashun and Bahali resisted, and the proposal was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 世祖親政，累進世職一等阿思哈尼哈番加拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: When the Shizu took personal rule, Hashun's hereditary rank was repeatedly advanced to first-class ashanihanafan with tashalahafan added.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Shizu Emperor assumed personal rule, Hashun's hereditary rank was restored and raised step by step to first-class ashanihanafan with an added tashalahafan.

sentences.zh: 十二年，獎奉職恪勤諸大臣，加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was among the diligent ministers in office who were rewarded and was given the additional title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12 he was honored among the dutiful ministers still in service and was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 康熙初卒，諡恪僖。

translations.literal: He died early in Kangxi and was given the posthumous name Keixi.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Kangxi reign and was posthumously titled Keixi.

sentences.zh: 米思翰，其長子也，襲世職，兼管牛錄，授內務府總管。

translations.literal: Mi Sihan was his eldest son; he inherited the hereditary rank, also managed the niru, and was appointed Superintendent of the Imperial Household Department.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Sihan, his eldest son, inherited the family rank, took charge of the niru as well, and was appointed superintendent of the Imperial Household Department.

sentences.zh: 輔政大臣從假尚方器物，力拒之。

translations.literal: The regent ministers asked to borrow imperial regalia; he firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: When the regent ministers sought to borrow objects from the imperial workshops, he firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 聖祖親政，知其守正，授禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: When the Sage Ancestor took personal rule, knowing his integrity, he was appointed Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After the Kangxi Emperor assumed personal rule, recognizing his integrity, he appointed Mi Sihan Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 八年，擢戶部尚書，列議政大臣。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was promoted to Minister of Revenue and enrolled among the Grand Councilors.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi year 8 he was promoted to Minister of Revenue and named a Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 是時各直省歲賦，聽布政使存留司庫，蠹弊相仍，米思翰疏請通飭各直省俸餉諸經費，所餘悉解部，由是勾稽出納權盡屬戶部。

translations.literal: At that time the annual levies of each province were left in provincial treasuries under the provincial treasurer, and abuses continued one after another; Mi Sihan memorialized requesting uniform orders to each province for salaries and all expenses, with the remainder all remitted to the ministry—thereby audit and disbursement authority came entirely under the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial grain taxes were then routinely kept in local treasuries under the provincial treasurer, and corruption persisted. Mi Sihan memorialized that salaries and all routine expenses in every province should be met from those funds and the surplus sent to the capital. Thereafter the Ministry of Revenue held full control over revenue and disbursement.

sentences.zh: 十二年，尚可喜疏請撤籓，吳三桂、耿精忠疏繼入，下戶、兵二部議。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Shang Kexi memorialized requesting withdrawal of his fief; memorials from Wu Sangui and Geng Jingzhong followed; the matter was referred to the Ministries of Revenue and War for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12 Shang Kexi memorialized asking to surrender his princely fief, and Wu Sangui and Geng Jingzhong soon sent similar requests. The court referred the matter to the Ministries of Revenue and War.

sentences.zh: 米思翰與兵部尚書明珠議三籓並撤，有言吳三桂不可撤者，以兩議入奏。

translations.literal: Mi Sihan and Minister of War Mingzhu held that all three feudatories should be abolished together; some said Wu Sangui must not be abolished—the two views were submitted to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Sihan and Minister of War Mingzhu argued that all three feudatories should be abolished at once, while others held that Wu Sangui must be left in place. Both positions were reported to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 复集諸大臣廷議，米思翰堅持宜並撤，議乃定。

translations.literal: The ministers were again assembled for court deliberation; Mi Sihan insisted that abolition should be simultaneous, and the decision was settled.
translations.idiomatic: The court convened the ministers again. Mi Sihan held firm that all three must be abolished together, and the policy was decided.

sentences.zh: 既而吳三桂反，上命王貝勒等率八旗兵討之，議者謂軍需浩繁，宜就近調兵禦守。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Wu Sangui rebelled; the emperor ordered princes and beile to lead the Eight Banners in campaign; deliberators said supplies would be vast and troops should be mobilized nearby for defense.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui soon rose in rebellion, and the emperor ordered princes and beile to lead the Eight Banners against him. Some argued that the war would be costly and that troops should be drawn from nearby garrisons for defense alone.

sentences.zh: 米思翰言：「賊勢猖獗，非綠旗兵所能製，宜以八旗勁旅會剿。

translations.literal: Mi Sihan said: "The rebels are fierce; Green Banner troops cannot subdue them—the strong forces of the Eight Banners should join in concerted suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Sihan said, "The rebels are too fierce for the Green Banner alone. We should commit the elite forces of the Eight Banners to a joint campaign.

sentences.zh: 軍需內外協濟，足支十年，可無他慮。」

translations.literal: Supplies can be coordinated within and without and will suffice for ten years—there need be no other worry."
translations.idiomatic: With resources pooled from court and provinces, we can sustain the war for ten years without other concern."

sentences.zh: 於是請以內府所儲分年發給，复綜覈各直省庫金、倉粟，以時撥運，悉稱旨。

translations.literal: He then requested that the inner treasury stores be issued year by year, and again audited gold in provincial treasuries and granary grain, allocating and transporting them on schedule—all accorded with the imperial will.
translations.idiomatic: He then proposed drawing on the inner treasury in annual allotments, auditing silver in provincial vaults and grain in state granaries, and shipping supplies on schedule. The emperor approved it all.

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「師行所至，屢奉明詔以正賦給軍需，恐有司尚多藉端私派，請敕各督撫嚴察所屬，供應糧餉薪芻，一切動官帑，毋許苛派；

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Wherever the army marches, repeated clear edicts have ordered that regular taxes supply military needs; I fear local officials still levy under many pretexts—please command each governor-general and governor to strictly inspect subordinates: grain, pay, fodder, and fuel for supply must all come from official funds, with no harsh exactions allowed;
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized, "Imperial edicts have repeatedly ordered that regular taxes fund the armies on campaign, yet local officials may still levy under one pretext or another. I ask that every governor-general and governor be instructed to supervise their subordinates strictly: grain, pay, fodder, and fuel must all come from official funds, with no harsh exactions permitted;

sentences.zh: 其購自民間者，務視時價支給，勿纖毫累民。」

translations.literal: what is purchased from the people must be paid at current prices, with not the slightest burden on the populace."
translations.idiomatic: whatever is bought from the people must be paid at fair market prices, without the slightest added burden on them."

sentences.zh: 上命如議速行。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered that the proposal be carried out at once.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the proposal implemented without delay.

sentences.zh: 米思翰尋卒，年甫四十三，上深惜之，予祭葬，諡敏果。

translations.literal: Mi Sihan soon died, aged only forty-three; the emperor deeply regretted it, granted funeral rites, and gave the posthumous name Minguo.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Sihan died soon after, at only forty-three. The emperor mourned him deeply, granted state funeral honors, and posthumously titled him Minguo.

sentences.zh: 時三桂勢方張，精忠及可喜子之信皆叛，議者追咎撤籓主議諸臣，上曰：「朕自少時，以三籓勢日熾，不可不撤。

translations.literal: At that time Wu Sangui's power was still rising; Jingzhong and Shang Kexi's son Zhixin had both rebelled; deliberators blamed the ministers who had advocated abolishing the fiefs; the emperor said: "From my youth I saw the Three Feudatories growing daily stronger and knew they could not be left in place.
translations.idiomatic: While Wu Sangui's power was still spreading and Geng Jingzhong and Shang Kexi's son Zhixin had also rebelled, critics blamed the ministers who had urged abolishing the feudatories. The emperor said, "Even as a young man I saw the Three Feudatories growing stronger every day and knew they had to be removed.

sentences.zh: 豈因其叛，諉過於人耶？」

translations.literal: How could I, because they rebelled, shift the blame onto others?"
translations.idiomatic: Am I to blame others because they rebelled?"

sentences.zh: 及事定，上追憶主議諸臣，猶稱米思翰不置。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, the emperor recalled the ministers who had led the policy and still spoke of Mi Sihan without end.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was crushed, the emperor looked back on the ministers who had led the policy and still spoke of Mi Sihan with unceasing praise.

sentences.zh: 米思翰子馬斯喀、馬齊、馬武，皆自有傳。

translations.literal: Mi Sihan's sons Maska, Maqi, and Mawu each have their own biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Sihan's sons Maska, Maqi, and Mawu are each treated in separate biographies.

sentences.zh: 李榮保，襲世職，兼管牛錄，累遷至察哈爾總管，卒。

translations.literal: Li Rongbao inherited the hereditary rank, also managed the niru, rose in succession to Chahar commandant, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Li Rongbao inherited the family rank, took charge of the niru as well, rose through the ranks to Chahar commandant, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二年，冊李榮保女為皇后，追封一等公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianlong, Li Rongbao's daughter was installed as empress and he was posthumously enfeoffed as a first-rank duke.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong year 2, Li Rongbao's daughter was made empress, and he was posthumously created a first-rank duke.

sentences.zh: 十三年，冊諡孝賢皇后，推恩先世，進封米思翰一等公。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year she was given the posthumous title Empress Xiaoxian; favor was extended to forebears and Mi Sihan was advanced to first-rank duke.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 she was given the posthumous title Empress Xiaoxian. Honors were extended to her forebears, and Mi Sihan was raised to first-rank duke.

sentences.zh: 十四年，以李榮保子大學士傅恆經略金川功，敕建宗祠，祀哈什屯、米思翰、李榮保，並追諡李榮保曰莊愨。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, on the merit of Li Rongbao's son, Grand Secretary Fu Heng, in pacifying Jinchuan, an imperial order built an ancestral hall enshrining Hashun, Mi Sihan, and Li Rongbao, and Li Rongbao was posthumously titled Zhuangque.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14, because Li Rongbao's son, Grand Secretary Fu Heng, had led the Jinchuan campaign to success, the court ordered an ancestral hall built to honor Hashun, Mi Sihan, and Li Rongbao, and Li Rongbao was posthumously titled Zhuangque.

sentences.zh: 顧八代，字文起，伊爾根覺羅氏，滿洲鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: Gu Badai, courtesy name Wenqi, of the Irgen Gioro clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Badai, whose courtesy name was Wenqi, of the Irgen Gioro clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 父顧納禪，事太宗，從伐明，次大同，攻小石城，先登，賜號「巴圖魯」，予世職牛錄章京。

translations.literal: His father Gunazan served the Taizong; campaigning against the Ming, below Datong he attacked Little Stone City, was first to scale the wall, and was granted the title "Baturu" and a hereditary office as niru janggin.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gunazan served the Taizong. On the campaign against the Ming, when the army halted at Datong, he stormed Little Stone City and was first over the wall. He was granted the title "Baturu" and a hereditary rank as niru janggin.

sentences.zh: 旋授甲喇額真。

translations.literal: He was soon appointed jalan commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed jalan commander.

sentences.zh: 順治初，從入關，定陝西、湖南、江南、浙江，皆在行間，進三等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: Early in Shunzhi he followed the entry into China, and in pacifying Shaanxi, Hunan, Jiangnan, and Zhejiang was always in the ranks, advancing to third-class adahahafan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shunzhi he entered China with the armies and took part in pacifying Shaanxi, Hunan, Jiangnan, and Zhejiang, rising to third-class adahahafan.

sentences.zh: 子顧蘇，襲，進二等。

translations.literal: His son Gusu inherited and advanced to second class.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gusu inherited the rank, which was raised to second class.

sentences.zh: 顧八代，其次子也。

translations.literal: Gu Badai was his second son.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Badai was his second son.

sentences.zh: 任俠重義，好讀書，善射。

translations.literal: Chivalrous and righteous, he loved reading and was skilled in archery.
translations.idiomatic: Bold and principled, he loved books and excelled at archery.

sentences.zh: 以廕生充護軍。

translations.literal: By yinsheng privilege he served as a guardsman.
translations.idiomatic: Through the yinsheng privilege he entered service as a guardsman.

sentences.zh: 順治十六年，從征雲南有功，授戶部筆帖式。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Shunzhi he followed the campaign to Yunnan with merit and was appointed a clerk in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi year 16 he campaigned in Yunnan with distinction and was appointed a clerk in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 旋以顧蘇及子佛岳相繼卒，無嗣，顧八代襲世職，遷吏部郎中。

translations.literal: Soon Gusu and his son Foyue died in succession without heirs; Gu Badai inherited the hereditary rank and was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Gusu and his son Foyue died in succession without heirs, so Gu Badai inherited the family rank and was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 康熙十四年，聖祖試旗員第一，擢翰林院侍讀學士。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Kangxi the Sage Ancestor tested banner officers and ranked him first, promoting him Reader in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi year 14 the emperor tested banner officers and ranked Gu Badai first, promoting him to Reader in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂陷湖南，遣其將掠兩廣。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui seized Hunan and sent his generals to raid the two Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui seized Hunan and sent his generals to ravage Guangdong and Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 鎮南將軍莽依圖自江西下廣東，駐韶州。

translations.literal: General of the South Manggitu advanced from Jiangxi into Guangdong and encamped at Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: General of the South Manggitu marched from Jiangxi into Guangdong and encamped at Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 十六年，上命顧八代傳諭莽依圖規复廣西，即留軍，從征廣西。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year the emperor ordered Gu Badai to convey instructions to Manggitu to recover Guangxi and to remain with the army in the Guangxi campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16 the emperor sent Gu Badai to instruct Manggitu to recover Guangxi and ordered him to remain with the army for the Guangxi campaign.

sentences.zh: 巡撫傅弘烈為三桂將吳世琮所敗，莽依圖引兵與相合。

translations.literal: Governor Fu Honglie was defeated by Wu Sangui's general Wu Shijiong; Manggitu led troops to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Fu Honglie was defeated by Wu Sangui's general Wu Shicong, and Manggitu marched to join forces with him.

sentences.zh: 顧八代按行諸軍，謂結營散亂，敵至慮不相應。

translations.literal: Gu Badai inspected the armies and said the scattered encampments would not respond to one another if the enemy came.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Badai inspected the armies and warned that with camps scattered so widely, the units could not support one another when the enemy struck.

sentences.zh: 世琮兵至，師复敗，還駐梧州。

translations.literal: When Shijiong's troops arrived the army was again defeated and withdrew to encamp at Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Shijiong's troops arrived the army was defeated again and fell back to Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 世琮來追，擊卻之。

translations.literal: Shijiong pursued; they struck and drove him back.
translations.idiomatic: Shijiong pursued, but they counterattacked and drove him off.

sentences.zh: 顧八代策世琮且復至，益誡備。

translations.literal: Gu Badai judged that Shijiong would return and urged greater readiness.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Badai expected Shijiong to return and urged the troops to prepare more carefully.

sentences.zh: 會除夕，世琮以三萬人奄至，又擊敗之。

translations.literal: It was New Year's Eve; Shijiong came suddenly with thirty thousand men and was again defeated.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Eve Shijiong struck with thirty thousand men and was defeated once more.

sentences.zh: 十七年，師進次盤江，與世琮軍遇，莽依圖病甚，以軍事屬顧八代；

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year the army advanced to Pan River and met Shijiong's force; Manggitu was gravely ill and entrusted military affairs to Gu Badai;
translations.idiomatic: In year 17 the army advanced to the Pan River and met Shijiong's force. Manggitu was gravely ill and entrusted command to Gu Badai;

sentences.zh: 偕副都統勒貝等渡江，與世琮戰，分兵出敵後，破其左而合擊其右。

translations.literal: with Vice Commander-in-chief Lebei and others he crossed the river and fought Shijiong, sending detachments around the enemy rear, breaking their left and striking their right in concert.
translations.idiomatic: With Vice Commander-in-chief Lebei and others he crossed the river and engaged Shijiong, sending detachments around the enemy rear while breaking their left flank and striking their right in concert.

sentences.zh: 世琮潰​​圍出，遣精騎追之，自殺。

translations.literal: Shijiong broke out of encirclement; elite cavalry pursued and he killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Shijiong broke out of the encirclement, but elite cavalry pursued him and he took his own life.

sentences.zh: 師進克南寧，叛將馬承廕與三桂軍合，可十萬，拒戰。

translations.literal: The army advanced and took Nanning; the rebel general Ma Chengzhao joined Wu Sangui's forces, numbering about one hundred thousand, and resisted.
translations.idiomatic: The army advanced and took Nanning. The rebel Ma Chengyin united with Wu Sangui's troops to some one hundred thousand men and offered battle.

sentences.zh: 諸將或難之，顧八代奮入陣，諸將皆力戰，遂破敵。

translations.literal: Some generals hesitated; Gu Badai charged into the formation and all the generals fought fiercely, and the enemy was broken.
translations.idiomatic: Some generals hesitated, but Gu Badai plunged into the enemy ranks. The others fought hard as well, and the rebel army was shattered.

sentences.zh: 十八年，京察，掌院學士拉薩里、葉方藹以顧八代從征有績效，注上考；

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, at the capital evaluation, Academician-in-Chief Lasali and Ye Fangyi noted Gu Badai's campaign achievements and entered him for top grade;
translations.idiomatic: In year 18, at the capital evaluation, Academicians-in-Chief Lasali and Ye Fangyi credited Gu Badai's campaign service and recommended him for top grade;

sentences.zh: 大學士索額圖改注「浮躁」，坐奪官。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Songgotu changed the entry to "frivolous" and he was dismissed from office on that charge.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Songgotu changed the entry to "frivolous," and on that charge Gu Badai was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 莽依圖疏言顧八代從征三載，竭誠奮勉，運籌決勝，請留軍委署副都統，參贊軍務，上命以原銜從征。

translations.literal: Manggitu memorialized that Gu Badai had served three years on campaign with utmost loyalty and effort, planning and deciding victories, and requested he remain with the army as acting Vice Commander-in-chief to assist in military affairs; the emperor ordered him to campaign at his former rank.
translations.idiomatic: Manggitu memorialized that Gu Badai had served three years on campaign with utmost loyalty, planning and winning battles, and asked that he remain as acting Vice Commander-in-chief to assist in military affairs. The emperor ordered him to continue at his former rank.

sentences.zh: 十九年，莽依圖卒於軍，顧八代從平南大將軍賚塔下雲南，攻會城。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year Manggitu died in the army; Gu Badai followed the Pacification of the South Grand General Ceben in the descent on Yunnan to attack the provincial capital.
translations.idiomatic: In year 19 Manggitu died in camp. Gu Badai followed Pacification of the South Grand General Laita south into Yunnan to besiege the provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 顧八代議當先取銀錠山，俯瞰城內，攻得勢。

translations.literal: Gu Badai argued that Silver Ingot Hill should be taken first to overlook the city within and gain the advantage in attack.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Badai argued that Silver Ingot Hill should be taken first so the city could be overlooked and the assault would gain the advantage.

sentences.zh: 及勇略將軍趙良棟師至，用顧八代策，先取銀錠山，克會城，雲南平。

translations.literal: When Brave Strategy General Zhao Liangdong's army arrived, Gu Badai's plan was adopted; Silver Ingot Hill was taken first, the provincial capital was taken, and Yunnan was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: When Brave Strategy General Zhao Liangdong's army arrived, they adopted Gu Badai's plan, took Silver Ingot Hill first, captured the capital, and pacified Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 師還，授侍講學士。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was appointed Expositor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned he was appointed Expositor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，命直尚書房，累遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was ordered to attend in the Imperial Study and was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In year 23 he was ordered to serve in the Imperial Study and was promoted in stages to Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，授尚書。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was appointed Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In year 28 he was appointed Minister.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，坐事，上責其不稱職，奪官，留世職，仍直尚書房。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he was charged with an offense; the emperor reproached him as unfit for office, stripped his post, retained his hereditary rank, and still had him attend in the Imperial Study.
translations.idiomatic: In year 32 he was charged with an offense. The emperor rebuked him as unfit for office, removed him from his post, but kept his hereditary rank and still had him attend in the Imperial Study.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，以病乞休。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year he begged leave on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In year 37 he requested retirement on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 四十七年，卒。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In year 47 he died.

sentences.zh: 顧八代直尚書房時，世宗從受學；

translations.literal: When Gu Badai attended the Imperial Study, the Shizong received instruction from him;
translations.idiomatic: While Gu Badai served in the Imperial Study, the future Yongzheng Emperor studied under him;

sentences.zh: 及卒，貧無以斂，世宗親臨奠，為經紀其喪。

translations.literal: when he died, his family was too poor to bury him; the Shizong came in person to offer mourning and arranged his funeral.
translations.idiomatic: When he died his family was too poor to bury him properly. The Yongzheng Emperor came in person to mourn and arranged the funeral.

sentences.zh: 雍正四年，詔复官，加太傅，予祭葬，諡文端，又以其貧，賜其家​​白金萬。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongzheng an edict restored his office, added Grand Tutor, granted funeral rites, posthumously titled Wenduan, and because of his poverty gave his family ten thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng year 4 an edict restored his office, made him Grand Tutor posthumously, granted state funeral honors, and gave him the posthumous title Wenduan. Because he had died poor, the court also gave his family ten thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 八年，建賢良祠京師，諭滿洲大臣當入祀者五人，大學士圖海、都統賚塔，次即顧八代，及尚書瑪爾漢、齊蘇勒。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the Worthy and Good Shrine was built in the capital; an edict named five Manchu ministers who should be enshrined—Grand Secretary Tulai and Commander-in-chief Ceben, next Gu Badai, and Ministers Ma Erhan and Qisuole.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 the Worthy and Good Shrine was built in the capital. An edict named five Manchu ministers for enshrinement: Grand Secretary Tulai and Commander-in-chief Ceben, then Gu Badai, and Ministers Ma Erhan and Qisuole.

sentences.zh: 子顧儼，襲世職，自參領官至副都統。

translations.literal: His son Gu Yan inherited the hereditary rank and rose from company commander to Vice Commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gu Yan inherited the family rank and rose from company commander to Vice Commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 孫顧琮，自有傳。

translations.literal: His grandson Gu Cong has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Gu Cong is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 瑪爾漢，兆佳氏，滿洲正白旗人。

translations.literal: Ma Erhan, of the Zhaojia clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Erhan, of the Zhaojia clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 順治十一年，繙譯舉人，授工部七品筆帖式，累遷刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Shunzhi he passed the translation juren examination and was appointed a seventh-rank clerk in the Ministry of Works, rising in succession to Vice Director in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi year 11 he passed the translation juren examination and was appointed a seventh-rank clerk in the Ministry of Works, rising in time to Vice Director in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 康熙十三年，陝西提督王輔臣叛應吳三桂，上命揚威將軍阿密達自江寧移師討之，瑪爾漢以署驍騎參領從。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kangxi Shaanxi Provincial Commander Wang Fuchen rebelled in support of Wu Sangui; the emperor ordered General of Might Yangwei Amida to move his army from Jiangning to suppress him, and Ma Erhan followed as acting cavalry company commander.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi year 13 the Shaanxi commander Wang Fuchen rebelled in support of Wu Sangui. The emperor ordered General of Might Amida to move his army from Jiangning against him, and Ma Erhan followed as acting cavalry company commander.

sentences.zh: 十四年，與副都統鄂克濟哈、穆舒琿等自涇州進兵，屢破壘，斬級數百，克寧州。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, with Vice Commander-in-chief Ekejiha, Mushuhu, and others he advanced from Jingzhou, repeatedly broke enemy stockades, beheaded several hundred, and took Ningzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14, with Vice Commander-in-chief Ekejiha, Mushuhu, and others, he advanced from Jingzhou, repeatedly stormed enemy stockades, slew several hundred, and captured Ningzhou.

sentences.zh: 十五年，大將軍圖海督兵圍平涼，輔臣降，瑪爾漢還京師。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Grand General Tulai supervised troops besieging Pingliang; Fuchen surrendered and Ma Erhan returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15 Grand General Tulai besieged Pingliang until Fuchen surrendered, and Ma Erhan returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 圖海請調涼州、寧夏、固原諸鎮兵進攻興安、漢中，上命副都統吳丹及瑪爾漢赴諸鎮料理徵發，兼詢緩急機宜。

translations.literal: Tulai requested that troops from Liangzhou, Ningxia, Guyuan, and other garrisons advance on Xing'an and Hanzhong; the emperor ordered Vice Commander-in-chief Wudan and Ma Erhan to go to the garrisons to manage levies and also inquire into urgent or leisurely strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Tulai asked to move troops from the Liangzhou, Ningxia, and Guyuan garrisons against Xing'an and Hanzhong. The emperor ordered Vice Commander-in-chief Wudan and Ma Erhan to the garrisons to organize levies and report on strategic priorities.

sentences.zh: 甘肅提督張勇請緩師，上命圖海固守鳳翔、秦州諸要隘，分兵授征南將軍穆佔下湖廣，命瑪爾漢從。

translations.literal: Gansu Provincial Commander Zhang Yong asked to slow the advance; the emperor ordered Tulai to hold the passes at Fengxiang, Qinzhou, and other key points, detach troops to General Who Campaigns South Muzhan's descent on Huguang, and ordered Ma Erhan to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Gansu commander Zhang Yong asked to delay the advance. The emperor ordered Tulai to hold the passes at Fengxiang, Qinzhou, and other key points, detach troops to General Muzhan's campaign in Huguang, and sent Ma Erhan with him.

sentences.zh: 十七年，授御史。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was appointed Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17 he was appointed censor.

sentences.zh: 十九年，穆佔師進貴州，二十年，師進雲南，瑪爾漢皆在行間，得功牌十二。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year Muzhan's army advanced into Guizhou; in the twentieth year the army advanced into Yunnan—Ma Erhan was in the ranks throughout and received twelve merit plaques.
translations.idiomatic: In year 19 Muzhan's army advanced into Guizhou, and in year 20 into Yunnan. Ma Erhan was with the army throughout and received twelve merit plaques.

sentences.zh: 雲南平，師還，追論徵湖南不力援永興，致損將士，奪功牌九。

translations.literal: When Yunnan was pacified and the army returned, a retrospective inquiry found that in the Hunan campaign he had failed to relieve Yongxing vigorously, causing loss of officers and men, and nine merit plaques were taken back.
translations.idiomatic: After Yunnan was pacified, a retrospective inquiry found that in the Hunan campaign he had failed to relieve Yongxing promptly, costing officers and men, and nine merit plaques were revoked.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，命巡視河東鹽政。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was ordered to inspect salt administration east of the river.
translations.idiomatic: In year 21 he was ordered to inspect salt administration east of the river.

sentences.zh: 御史許承宣、羅秉倫劾山西巡撫圖克善令平陽屬十三州縣增報鹽丁加課累民，下巡撫穆爾賽會瑪爾漢覈實，請免虛報一萬七千餘丁。

translations.literal: Censors Xu Chengxuan and Luo Binglun impeached Shanxi Governor Tukeshan for ordering thirteen prefectures and counties under Pingyang to report extra salt laborers and increase levies to burden the people; the matter was referred to Governor Muerse to verify with Ma Erhan, and they requested exemption for more than seventeen thousand falsely reported laborers.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Xu Chengxuan and Luo Binglun impeached Shanxi Governor Tukeshan for ordering thirteen subordinate districts under Pingyang to report extra salt laborers and raise levies, burdening the people. Governor Muerse was ordered to verify with Ma Erhan, and they recommended exempting more than seventeen thousand falsely reported laborers.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，以按治歸化城都統固穆德不實，吏議左遷。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, for an inadequate investigation of Commander-in-chief Gumude at Guihua, the personnel office recommended demotion.
translations.idiomatic: In year 25, for an inadequate investigation of Commander-in-chief Gumude at Guihua, the personnel office recommended demotion.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，授理籓院司務。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was appointed Secretary of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In year 26 he was appointed Secretary of the Court of Colonial Affairs.

sentences.zh: 從大學士索額圖等使鄂羅斯定邊界，辭辨明析，鄂羅斯人折服。

translations.literal: Following Grand Secretary Songgotu and others on a mission to Russia to fix the border, his arguments were clear and the Russians were convinced.
translations.idiomatic: On a mission with Grand Secretary Songgotu and others to Russia to fix the border, his arguments were lucid and the Russians were convinced.

sentences.zh: 事聞，聖祖嘉其能。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, the Sage Ancestor praised his ability.
translations.idiomatic: When the report reached court, the Kangxi Emperor praised his ability.

sentences.zh: 尋遷戶部郎中。

translations.literal: He was soon transferred to Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，遷翰林院侍講學士，再遷兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he was transferred to Expositor in the Hanlin Academy and again promoted to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In year 33 he was transferred to Expositor in the Hanlin Academy and soon promoted again to Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，上親征噶爾丹，命瑪爾漢駐土木董理驛站，以送軍馬羸，吏議奪官，命寬之。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year the emperor campaigned in person against Galdan and ordered Ma Erhan to remain at Tumu to oversee relay stations; because the army horses sent were weak, the personnel office recommended stripping his office, but the emperor ordered leniency.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi year 35 the emperor campaigned in person against Galdan and stationed Ma Erhan at Tumu to manage relay posts. Because the army horses supplied were in poor condition, the personnel office recommended dismissal, but the emperor showed leniency.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，遷左都御史。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year he was transferred to Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In year 38 he was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 再遷兵部尚書，充經筵講官、議政大臣。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Minister of War, appointed lecturer at the Classics Colloquium, and enrolled among the Deliberative Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to Minister of War, made a lecturer at the Classics Colloquium, and named a Deliberative Minister.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，歲饑，流民就食京師。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year there was famine and displaced people came to the capital for food.
translations.idiomatic: In year 43 famine struck, and refugees flocked to the capital for relief.

sentences.zh: 命與內大臣佟國維、明珠、阿密達等監賑。

translations.literal: He was ordered to supervise relief distribution with Grand Ministers of the Imperial Household Tong Guowei, Mingzhu, Amida, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to supervise famine relief with Grand Ministers Tong Guowei, Mingzhu, Amida, and others.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，調吏部。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In year 46 he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 四十八年，以老病乞休。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year he begged leave to retire on grounds of age and illness.
translations.idiomatic: In year 48 he requested retirement on grounds of age and illness.

sentences.zh: 五十七年，卒，年八十五。

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year he died, aged eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In year 57 he died at eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 上遣內大臣臨奠，賜祭葬。

translations.literal: The emperor sent a Grand Minister of the Imperial Household to offer mourning and granted funeral rites.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a grand minister to mourn on his behalf and granted state funeral honors.

sentences.zh: 雍正八年，世宗諭獎瑪爾漢謹慎忠厚，事聖祖宣力多年，完名引退，贈太子太傅。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yongzheng the Shizong issued an edict praising Ma Erhan's prudence and loyalty, his many years of service to the Sage Ancestor, and his honorable retirement, and posthumously made him Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng year 8 the Yongzheng Emperor praised Ma Erhan's prudence and loyalty, his long service to the Kangxi Emperor, and his honorable retirement, and posthumously made him Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 賢良祠成，命入祀。

translations.literal: When the Worthy and Good Shrine was completed, he was ordered enshrined.
translations.idiomatic: When the Worthy and Good Shrine was completed, he was ordered enshrined there.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，高宗命追諡恭勤。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong the Gaozong ordered the posthumous title Gongqin.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianlong the Qianlong Emperor ordered the posthumous title Gongqin.

sentences.zh: 田六善，字兼山，山西陽城人。

translations.literal: Tian Liushan, courtesy name Jianshan, was a native of Yangcheng in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Liushan, whose courtesy name was Jianshan, came from Yangcheng in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 順治三年進士，授河南太康知縣，時當兵後，勞來安集。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the third year of Shunzhi, he was appointed magistrate of Taikang in Henan; the region had just suffered war, and he labored to console and settle the people.
translations.idiomatic: A Shunzhi year 3 jinshi, he was appointed magistrate of Taikang in Henan. The district had just emerged from war, and he worked to console the people and restore order.

sentences.zh: 九年，巡撫吳景道疏薦才守兼優，遷戶部主事，監臨清關，复監鳳陽倉兼臨淮關。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Governor Wu Jingdao memorialized recommending his talent and integrity together; he was transferred to Principal Clerk in the Ministry of Revenue, supervised Linqing Pass, and again supervised Fengyang Granary while also overseeing Linhuai Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 Governor Wu Jingdao memorialized praising his combined talent and integrity. He was transferred to principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue, supervised Linqing Pass, and later Fengyang Granary together with Linhuai Pass.

sentences.zh: 罷濫徵，革奇羨，商民稱便。

translations.literal: He abolished excessive levies and eliminated irregular surcharges; merchants praised the convenience.
translations.idiomatic: He ended abusive levies and irregular surcharges, to the great relief of merchants.

sentences.zh: 累遷郎中。

translations.literal: He rose in succession to Director.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in stages to director.

sentences.zh: 十五年，授江南道御史。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was appointed Censor of the Jiangnan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15 he was appointed censor of the Jiangnan circuit.

sentences.zh: 兵部議禁民乘馬，六善疏言其不便，下廷臣集議，弛禁。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War deliberated banning commoners from riding horses; Liushan memorialized that this was inconvenient, the matter was referred to court ministers for joint deliberation, and the ban was relaxed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ministry of War proposed banning commoners from riding horses, Liushan memorialized that the measure was impractical. The court deliberated and relaxed the ban.

sentences.zh: 十六年，疏言：「欲安民在勸清吏，乞敕各督撫實行薦舉，吏部於各督撫蒞任一二年後，列奏薦舉何人，能否察吏安民，即可以是鑑別。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he memorialized: "To settle the people one must encourage upright officials. I beg that each governor-general and governor be ordered to carry out recommendations in earnest, and that after one or two years in office each governor-general and governor report whom he has recommended and whether he can inspect officials and settle the people—by this one may judge.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16 he memorialized, "To secure the people's welfare one must encourage upright officials. I ask that every governor-general and governor be ordered to recommend them in earnest, and that after one or two years in post each report whom he has recommended and whether he can inspect officials and keep the people at peace—by that one may judge their fitness.

sentences.zh: 議者或謂舉薦清吏，無以處乎不在清吏之列者，一難也；

translations.literal: Some deliberators said that recommending upright officials gives no place to those not among the upright—a first difficulty;
translations.idiomatic: Some objected that recommending upright officials leaves no place for those not so labeled—the first difficulty;

sentences.zh: 恐督撫依舊受賄徇私，二難也；

translations.literal: they feared governors-general and governors would still take bribes and show favoritism—a second difficulty;
translations.idiomatic: they feared governors-general and governors would still take bribes and show favoritism—the second difficulty;

sentences.zh: 徵糧緝逃處分罣礙，三難也。

translations.literal: and that penalties for grain collection and pursuit of fugitives would be obstructed—a third difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: and that penalties tied to tax collection and pursuit of fugitives would be obstructed—the third difficulty.

sentences.zh: 然臣謂清吏果得薦舉，則為清吏者見公道尚存，益堅其持守，一便也；

translations.literal: Yet I say that if upright officials are truly recommended, those who are upright will see that fairness still exists and will hold all the firmer to their conduct—a first advantage;
translations.idiomatic: Yet I hold that if upright officials are truly recommended, the upright will see that fairness still exists and will hold all the firmer to their standards—the first advantage;

sentences.zh: 群吏以不著清名為愧，力自濯磨，二便也；

translations.literal: the mass of officials will be ashamed not to have a clean name and will strive to improve themselves—a second advantage;
translations.idiomatic: other officials will be ashamed to lack a clean reputation and will strive to improve—the second advantage;

sentences.zh: 某省有清吏幾人，以驗政治修廢，三便也；

translations.literal: how many upright officials a province has will test whether government flourishes or declines—a third advantage;
translations.idiomatic: how many upright officials each province has will show whether its government flourishes or fails—the third advantage;

sentences.zh: 天下曉然知有能必先有守，風俗丕變，四便也；

translations.literal: all under Heaven will clearly know that ability must rest on integrity, and customs will greatly change—a fourth advantage;
translations.idiomatic: the empire will plainly see that ability must rest on integrity, and customs will be transformed—the fourth advantage;

sentences.zh: 向日督撫厭憎清吏無益於己，今必且卵翼而親愛之，五便也。

translations.literal: whereas governors-general and governors once detested upright officials as useless to themselves, they will now surely shelter and cherish them—a fifth advantage.
translations.idiomatic: whereas governors-general and governors once despised upright officials as useless to themselves, they will now shelter and value them—the fifth advantage.

sentences.zh: 不惑於三難，力致其五便，將循良興起，不讓前古矣。」

translations.literal: Not misled by the three difficulties but striving for the five advantages, worthy local officials will rise and not fall short of antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: Undeterred by the three difficulties and pressing for the five advantages, worthy local officials will arise and not fall short of antiquity."

sentences.zh: 下部議行。

translations.literal: The memorial was referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the ministries and carried out.

sentences.zh: 尋命巡視長蘆鹽政。

translations.literal: He was soon ordered to inspect the Changlu salt administration.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to inspect the Changlu salt administration.

sentences.zh: 十七年，還掌江南道事。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he returned to handle affairs of the Jiangnan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17 he resumed charge of the Jiangnan circuit.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，乞假歸。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi he begged leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kangxi he took leave to return home.

sentences.zh: 三年，補貴州道御史。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed Censor of the Guizhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he was appointed censor of the Guizhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 四年，疏言：「兵部議裁山西、陝西、河南等處兵額，三營裁一營。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he memorialized: "The Ministry of War has deliberated reducing troop quotas in Shanxi, Shaanxi, Henan, and other places, cutting one camp in three.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he memorialized, "The Ministry of War has deliberated reducing troop quotas in Shanxi, Shaanxi, Henan, and elsewhere, disbanding one camp in every three.

sentences.zh: 遇裁之兵，挾久練之技，處坐困之時，窮無所歸，遂為賊盜。

translations.literal: When troops are cut, they possess long-trained skills yet sit in constrained circumstances with nowhere to turn, and so become bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers who are cut retain long-trained skills yet find themselves idle and destitute, with nowhere to turn, and so become bandits.

sentences.zh: 請諭總督、提督諸臣，察已裁之兵，如弓馬嫻熟、膂力精強，仍收入伍。

translations.literal: I ask that governors-general and provincial commanders be instructed to examine troops already cut off: if skilled in bow and horse and strong in body, let them still be enrolled.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that governors-general and commanders examine discharged soldiers: if skilled in bow and horse and strong in body, let them be kept in the ranks.

sentences.zh: 自後老弱必斥，逃亡不補。

translations.literal: Hereafter the old and weak must be expelled and deserters not replaced.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward only the old and weak should be expelled, and deserters should not be replaced.

sentences.zh: 所漸去者疲卒，不慮其為非；

translations.literal: What is gradually removed will be worn-out soldiers, with no fear that they will turn to crime;
translations.idiomatic: What is gradually removed will be worn-out soldiers, with no fear that they will turn to crime;

sentences.zh: 所招回者勁兵，可資其實用。」

translations.literal: what is brought back will be strong troops who can serve practical use."
translations.idiomatic: what is brought back will be strong troops of real use."

sentences.zh: 下部議，令各營汰去老弱，其年力精壯者仍留充伍。

translations.literal: The memorial was referred to the ministries; each camp was ordered to eliminate the old and weak, while those still vigorous in years were retained in the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the ministries, which ordered each camp to eliminate the old and weak while retaining men still vigorous in years.

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「吏部於往日曾行之事，率皆援以為例，惟意所彼此，莫窮其弊。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "The Ministry of Personnel, regarding matters once carried out in the past, invariably cites them as precedent, favoring whichever side it wishes, so that the harm cannot be exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized, "The Ministry of Personnel, whenever something was once done in the past, cites it as precedent as it pleases, so that the harm cannot be exhausted.

sentences.zh: 請敕部以上所裁定及有旨著為例者，彙為一冊，敬謹遵守，餘仍循舊章。」

translations.literal: I ask that the ministry be commanded to compile into one volume all rulings it has decided and all matters the emperor has ordered made precedent, to be reverently observed, while the rest still follow the old regulations."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the ministry compile into one volume every ruling it has made and every matter the emperor has ordered made precedent, to be reverently observed, while the rest still follow the old regulations."

sentences.zh: 得旨，如所請。

translations.literal: An imperial rescript approved the request.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the request.

sentences.zh: 七年，命巡視京、通倉，還掌山東道事，得旨內升，回籍待缺。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was ordered to inspect the capital and Tongzhou granaries; on returning he resumed charge of the Shandong circuit and received an order for internal promotion, returning home to await a vacancy.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he was ordered to inspect the capital and Tongzhou granaries. On returning he resumed the Shandong circuit and received an order for internal promotion, then went home to await a vacancy.

sentences.zh: 十一年，授刑科給事中，秩視正四品。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was appointed Supervising Censor of the Penal Branch, with rank equivalent to regular fourth grade.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 he was appointed supervising censor of the Penal Branch, with rank equivalent to regular fourth grade.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「臣里居讀上諭，以蘇克薩哈為鼇拜仇陷，殺其子孫，連坐族人白爾赫圖，恩予昭雪。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "At home I read the imperial edict clearing Suksaha, who was framed and destroyed by Oboi out of enmity, killing his sons and grandsons and implicating the clansman Bai'erhetu by association.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized, "At home I read the imperial edict clearing Suksaha, whom Oboi destroyed out of enmity, killing his sons and grandsons and implicating the clansman Bai'erhetu by association.

sentences.zh: 臣思法律為天下共者也，以滿洲勞苦功高之人，因與執政諸臣意見相左，輒牽連興大獄，恐尤而效之，報復相尋，藉端推刃。

translations.literal: I reflect that law is what the realm shares in common. Because Manchus who toiled with high merit differed in opinion from those in power, great cases were repeatedly stirred up—I fear others will take this as a model, revenge will follow revenge, and blades will be drawn on any pretext.
translations.idiomatic: I reflect that law is what the whole realm shares. When meritorious Manchus who had borne hardship differed in opinion from those in power, great cases were stirred up repeatedly. I fear others will take this as a model, revenge will breed revenge, and any pretext will draw the blade.

sentences.zh: 周禮有八議，罪大可減，罪小可赦。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou provide the Eight Considerations: great crimes may be reduced, small crimes may be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou provide the Eight Considerations: great crimes may be mitigated and small crimes pardoned.

sentences.zh: 請特製昭示，滿洲犯罪非反叛有實蹟者，一準於律，勿妄議株連。

translations.literal: I ask for a special proclamation that for Manchu crimes, unless rebellion is proved by solid evidence, all shall follow the code and no one shall rashly propose implicating others by association.
translations.idiomatic: I ask for a special proclamation that for Manchu crimes, unless rebellion is proved by solid evidence, all shall follow the code and no one shall rashly propose collective punishment.

sentences.zh: 儲人才，固國本，於是乎在。」

translations.literal: To store up talent and secure the foundation of the state lies herein."
translations.idiomatic: To store up talent and secure the foundation of the state lies herein."

sentences.zh: 上韙其言，下王大臣議，從之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words and referred them to the princes and ministers for deliberation; they assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his words, referred them to the princes and ministers, and they assented.

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「聖學宜先讀史。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "The sage's learning should begin with reading history.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized, "The sage's learning should begin with reading history.

sentences.zh: 史者，古帝王得失之林也。

translations.literal: History is the forest of the gains and losses of ancient emperors.
translations.idiomatic: History is the forest in which the gains and losses of ancient emperors may be seen.

sentences.zh: 其君寬仁明斷，崇儉納諫，則其民必安，其事必治，其世必興必平。

translations.literal: If the ruler is generous, benevolent, clear, and decisive, honors frugality and accepts remonstrance, then the people will surely be secure, affairs will surely be governed, and the age will surely rise and be at peace.
translations.idiomatic: If the ruler is generous, benevolent, clear, and decisive, honors frugality, and accepts remonstrance, the people will be secure, affairs well governed, and the age will rise toward peace.

sentences.zh: 若夫苛察因循，惡聞過，樂逞欲，其民必不安，其事必不治，其世必衰必亂。

translations.literal: If he is harsh and scrutinizing, perfunctory and inert, hates to hear of faults, and delights in indulging desire, then the people will surely be insecure, affairs will surely be ungoverned, and the age will surely decline and fall into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: If he is harsh and scrutinizing, perfunctory and inert, hates to hear of faults, and indulges his desires, the people will be insecure, affairs ungoverned, and the age will decline into disorder.

sentences.zh: 乞諭日講諸臣，以通鑑與經史並進。」

translations.literal: I beg that the daily lecturers be instructed to advance the Comprehensive Mirror together with the classics and histories."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the daily lecturers be instructed to study the Comprehensive Mirror alongside the classics and histories."

sentences.zh: 得旨俞允。

translations.literal: An imperial rescript approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 尋轉戶科掌印給事中。

translations.literal: He was soon transferred to Supervising Censor of the Revenue Branch with seal authority.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to supervising censor of the Revenue Branch with seal authority.

sentences.zh: 三遷至右僉都御史。

translations.literal: After three promotions he reached Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: After three promotions he reached Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 十三年，疏言：「吳三桂負恩叛逆，處必滅之勢。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he memorialized: "Wu Sangui has betrayed his benefactor and rebelled and is in a position that must be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 he memorialized, "Wu Sangui has betrayed his benefactor and rebelled; he is in a position that must be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 綠旗月餉，步兵一兩有奇，馬兵二兩有奇，甲胄不必堅強，弓刀不必精利，登山涉水，資以先驅。

translations.literal: Green Banner monthly pay is a little over one tael for foot soldiers and a little over two for horsemen; armor need not be especially strong, bows and blades need not be especially sharp—they scale mountains and cross rivers and serve as vanguards.
translations.idiomatic: Green Banner monthly pay is a little over one tael for foot soldiers and over two for horsemen. Their armor need not be especially strong nor their weapons especially sharp; they scale mountains and ford rivers and serve as vanguards.

sentences.zh: 臣謂綠旗力雖弱，善用之則強；

translations.literal: I say that though Green Banner strength is weak, used well it becomes strong;
translations.idiomatic: I say that though the Green Banner is weak, used well it becomes strong;

sentences.zh: 心雖渙，善收之則聚。

translations.literal: though their hearts are scattered, gathered well they unite.
translations.idiomatic: though their hearts are scattered, gathered well they unite.

sentences.zh: 供給宜足，勞逸宜均。

translations.literal: Supply should be ample and labor and rest evenly apportioned.
translations.idiomatic: Supplies should be ample and labor and rest evenly apportioned.

sentences.zh: 至先登破陣，無分滿、漢，賞賚公平。

translations.literal: For leading the assault and breaking the enemy line, whether Manchu or Han, rewards and grants should be fair.
translations.idiomatic: For leading assaults and breaking enemy lines, whether Manchu or Han, rewards should be fair.

sentences.zh: 斯忠勇自奮，克佐勁旅以奏膚功，今日所宜急計者也。」

translations.literal: Then loyalty and courage will spur themselves forth, and they can assist the crack forces to achieve glorious merit—this is what should be urgently planned today."
translations.idiomatic: Then loyalty and courage will rise of themselves, and they can assist the crack forces to win glorious merit—this is what must be planned urgently today."

sentences.zh: 下部議鼓勵綠旗官兵敘給爵賞例。

translations.literal: The memorial was referred to the ministries, which deliberated regulations encouraging Green Banner officers and men with enfeoffment and rewards for merit.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the ministries, which deliberated regulations to encourage Green Banner officers and men with titles and rewards.

sentences.zh: 遷順天府尹。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Prefect of Shuntian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Prefect of Shuntian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 未幾，复遷左副都御史。

translations.literal: Before long he was again transferred to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred again to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 十四年，疏言：「臣昔為河南知縣時，孫可望、李定國尚據云、貴、四川，其勢不減於吳三桂。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he memorialized: "When I was a county magistrate in Henan, Sun Kewang and Li Dingguo still held Yunnan, Guizhou, and Sichuan, and their power was no less than Wu Sangui's.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14 he memorialized, "When I was a county magistrate in Henan, Sun Kewang and Li Dingguo still held Yunnan, Guizhou, and Sichuan, and their power was no less than Wu Sangui's.

sentences.zh: 金聲桓叛江西，姜瓖叛大同，亦不異耿精忠、王輔臣。

translations.literal: Jin Shenghuan rebelled in Jiangxi and Jiang Xiang in Datong—no different from Geng Jingzhong and Wang Fuchen.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Shenghuan rebelled in Jiangxi and Jiang Xiang in Datong—no different from Geng Jingzhong and Wang Fuchen.

sentences.zh: 而當日民心未若今之驚惶疑懼者，由其時督撫有孟喬芳、張存仁、吳景道諸臣，敦行儉樸，慎守廉隅，吏治肅清，民生樂遂也。

translations.literal: Yet the people's hearts then were not so alarmed and fearful as today, because at that time the governors-general had ministers such as Meng Qiaofang, Zhang Cunren, and Wu Jingdao, who practiced frugality in earnest, carefully guarded integrity, made officialdom austere, and let the people live content.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the people's hearts were not then so alarmed as today, because governors-general such as Meng Qiaofang, Zhang Cunren, and Wu Jingdao practiced frugality in earnest, guarded their integrity, kept officialdom austere, and let the people live in peace.

sentences.zh: 宜特頒嚴諭，令各督撫禁雜派，覈軍實。

translations.literal: It is fitting to issue a stern edict ordering each governor-general and governor to forbid miscellaneous levies and verify military strength.
translations.idiomatic: It is fitting to issue a stern edict ordering every governor-general and governor to forbid miscellaneous levies and verify true military strength.

sentences.zh: 有司或剝民敗檢，立行糾劾，以省民力、安眾心。

translations.literal: If local officials strip the people or fail in conduct, impeach them at once to spare the people's strength and settle their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: If local officials exploit the people or fail in conduct, impeach them at once to spare the people's strength and settle their hearts.

sentences.zh: 師行所至，更宜審酌剿禦。

translations.literal: Where the army marches, it is still more fitting to weigh suppression and defense carefully.
translations.idiomatic: Where armies march, it is still more important to weigh suppression and defense carefully.

sentences.zh: 近見江西、浙江報捷諸疏，屢言殺賊累萬。

translations.literal: Recently in victory reports from Jiangxi and Zhejiang it is repeatedly said that tens of thousands of bandits were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Recently victory reports from Jiangxi and Zhejiang repeatedly claim tens of thousands of bandits killed.

sentences.zh: 然必待殺盡而後入閩，恐愚頑之民無盡，草竊之賊亦無盡。

translations.literal: Yet if one must kill them all before entering Fujian, I fear the foolish and obstinate among the people are endless, and grass-bandit thieves are also endless.
translations.idiomatic: Yet if one must kill them all before entering Fujian, the foolish and obstinate among the people are endless, and grass-bandit thieves are endless as well.

sentences.zh: 臣謂先取精忠，則群賊自息。

translations.literal: I say that if Jingzhong is taken first, the other bandits will cease of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: I say that if Jingzhong is taken first, the other bandits will cease of themselves.

sentences.zh: 昔姜瓖乍叛，土寇群起，瓖滅，土寇亦盡，其明驗也。

translations.literal: In the past when Jiang Xian first rebelled, local bandits rose in groups; when Jiang was destroyed, the local bandits were also exhausted—this is clear proof.
translations.idiomatic: In the past when Jiang Xian first rebelled, local bandits rose everywhere; when Jiang fell, the local bandits vanished as well—clear proof.

sentences.zh: 至三桂狡謀，覬以一隅之地困天下全力，我即以天下全力困此一隅。

translations.literal: As for Wu Sangui's crafty plot, he hopes to weary the empire's full strength with one corner; we should weary this one corner with the empire's full strength.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui's crafty plot is to weary the empire's full strength with one corner; we should weary that corner with the empire's full strength.

sentences.zh: 三桂授首，則四川、廣西不煩兵而自定。」

translations.literal: When Wu Sangui loses his head, Sichuan and Guangxi will need no troops and will settle of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui falls, Sichuan and Guangxi will need no armies and will settle of themselves."

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「臣籍山西，與陝西接壤。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "My native place is Shanxi, adjoining Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized, "My native place is Shanxi, adjoining Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 黃河自邊外折入內地，至蒲州一千餘裡。

translations.literal: The Yellow River bends in from beyond the border to the interior, more than a thousand li to Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River bends in from beyond the border to the interior, more than a thousand li to Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 蒲州上至禹門，為平陽府屬，河西為西安，有提督、總兵重兵駐守。

translations.literal: From Puzhou up to Yumen Gate is under Pingyang Prefecture; west of the river is Xi'an, where a provincial commander and regional commander with heavy troops are stationed.
translations.idiomatic: From Puzhou up to Yumen Gate is under Pingyang Prefecture. West of the river is Xi'an, where a provincial commander and regional commander keep heavy troops.

sentences.zh: 自此以北，永寧州、臨縣為汾州府屬，渡口有孟門鎮、高家塔諸處；

translations.literal: North of this, Yongning Prefecture and Lin County are under Fenzhou Prefecture; at the crossings are Mengmen Town, Gaojia Tower, and other places;
translations.idiomatic: Farther north, Yongning Prefecture and Lin County are under Fenzhou Prefecture; at the crossings are Mengmen Town, Gaojia Tower, and other places;

sentences.zh: 更北保德州為太原府屬，渡口有黑田溝、窮狼窩諸處。

translations.literal: still farther north, Baode Prefecture is under Taiyuan Prefecture, with crossings at Heitian Ditch, Qionglangwo, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: still farther north, Baode Prefecture is under Taiyuan Prefecture, with crossings at Heitian Ditch, Qionglangwo, and other places.

sentences.zh: 河西為延安，素稱荒野，河東為交城，路險山深，草竊潛匿。

translations.literal: West of the river is Yan'an, long called a wilderness; east of the river is Jiaocheng, with dangerous roads and deep mountains where grass-bandits lie hidden.
translations.idiomatic: West of the river is Yan'an, long called a wilderness; east of the river is Jiaocheng, with dangerous roads and deep mountains where bandits lie hidden.

sentences.zh: 請敕巡撫、提督分兵駐防。」

translations.literal: I ask that governors and commanders be commanded to detach troops for garrison defense."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that governors and commanders be ordered to detach troops for garrison defense."

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「師已抵平涼，輔臣迫於必死，困獸猶鬥，殺賊百不償失兵一。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "The army has reached Pingliang; Fuchen is driven to certain death and fights like a cornered beast—a hundred enemies killed do not repay the loss of one soldier.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized, "The army has reached Pingliang. Fuchen is driven to certain death and fights like a cornered beast; a hundred enemies killed do not repay the loss of one soldier.

sentences.zh: 宜駐軍城下，以逸待勞，急攻固原，絕其糧道。

translations.literal: It is fitting to encamp below the city and await the weary with ease, and press the attack on Guyuan to cut his grain route.
translations.idiomatic: It is fitting to encamp below the city and await the weary with ease, and press the attack on Guyuan to cut his grain route.

sentences.zh: 平涼地瘠，非比湖南地廣米多，可以持久。

translations.literal: Pingliang's land is poor, unlike Hunan's broad territory and abundant rice, where one can endure long.
translations.idiomatic: Pingliang's land is poor, unlike Hunan's broad territory and abundant grain, where one can endure long.

sentences.zh: 糧道不通，人心自散，必有斬輔臣獻軍門者。

translations.literal: If the grain route is cut, hearts will scatter of themselves, and there will surely be those who behead Fuchen and present him at the army gate.
translations.idiomatic: If the grain route is cut, hearts will scatter of themselves, and someone will surely behead Fuchen and present him at the army gate.

sentences.zh: 若賊東出則東應，賊西出則西應，疲我師徒，分我威力，固原圍解，賊氣貫通，此斷斷不可者也。」

translations.literal: If bandits come out east the army responds east; if they come out west it responds west—wearing out our forces and dividing our power, the siege of Guyuan is lifted and rebel spirit runs through—this is absolutely not to be done."
translations.idiomatic: If bandits move east the army responds east and if west then west, wearing out our forces and dividing our power, the siege of Guyuan is lifted and rebel spirit runs through—this must absolutely not be done."

sentences.zh: 諸疏並下王大臣議行。

translations.literal: All the memorials were referred to the princes and ministers for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: All the memorials were referred to the princes and ministers and carried out.

sentences.zh: 十六年，擢工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was promoted to Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16 he was promoted to Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 十七年，以夏旱求言，疏言：「今日官至督撫，居莫敢誰何之勢，自非大賢，鮮不縱恣。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, when drought in summer prompted a call for advice, he memorialized: "Today officials who reach the rank of governor-general occupy a position none dare challenge; unless they are great worthies, few do not indulge themselves.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17, when summer drought prompted a call for advice, he memorialized, "Today officials who reach governor-general stand where none dare challenge them; unless they are great worthies, few refrain from excess.

sentences.zh: 道府歲納規禮，加之以搜括，則道府所轄官民，不啻鬻之道府矣。

translations.literal: Circuits and prefectures pay annual customary gifts, and with additional squeezing the officials and people under the circuits and prefectures are no better than sold to them.
translations.idiomatic: Circuits and prefectures pay annual customary gifts, and with additional squeezing the officials and people under them are virtually sold to those circuits and prefectures.

sentences.zh: 州縣歲納規禮，重之以勒索，則州縣所屬士民，不啻鬻之州縣矣。

translations.literal: Departments and counties pay annual customary gifts, and with further extortion the gentry and people belonging to them are no better than sold to the departments and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Departments and counties pay annual customary gifts, and with further extortion the gentry and people under them are virtually sold to those departments and counties.

sentences.zh: 世祖朝，山東巡按程衡劾巡撫耿焞，江南巡按秦世禎劾土國寶，皆置重典，天下肅然。

translations.literal: In the Shizu reign, Shandong Regional Inspector Cheng Heng impeached Governor Geng Tun, and Jiangnan Regional Inspector Qin Shizhen impeached Tu Guobao—both received heavy punishment, and all under Heaven were awed.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shunzhi reign, Shandong regional inspector Cheng Heng impeached Governor Geng Tun, and Jiangnan regional inspector Qin Shizhen impeached Tu Guobao—both received heavy punishment, and the empire was awed.

sentences.zh: 今巡按久停，雖欲議复，恐一時難得多人。

translations.literal: Today surveillance commissioners have long been suspended; though one wishes to deliberate restoring them, I fear it will be hard to find many qualified men at once.
translations.idiomatic: Surveillance commissioners have long been suspended; though one might wish to restore them, it will be hard to find enough qualified men at once.

sentences.zh: 惟有出自上意，欲清一省，則選一人遣往，不必一時俱發。

translations.literal: Only if it comes from the emperor's own intent, wishing to cleanse a province, should one man be chosen and sent—there is no need to dispatch them all at once.
translations.idiomatic: Only if the emperor himself wishes to cleanse a province should one man be chosen and sent; there is no need to dispatch them all at once.

sentences.zh: 出其不意，示以不測，使天下奸惡吏不敢恃督撫而肆志，即有不肖之督撫，亦莫敢庇貪而害民。」

translations.literal: Taking the enemy unawares and showing unpredictable action will make corrupt officials under Heaven not dare rely on governors-general and governors to indulge their will; even unworthy governors-general will not dare shield the greedy and harm the people."
translations.idiomatic: Striking without warning and showing unpredictable resolve will make corrupt officials everywhere afraid to rely on governors-general for license; even unworthy governors-general will not dare shield the greedy and harm the people."

sentences.zh: 疏入，報聞。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, acknowledgment was returned.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was received and acknowledged.

sentences.zh: 調戶部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 十八年，疏言：「國家有錢法以通有無、利民用，自秦、漢及唐、宋，公私皆悉用錢；

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he memorialized: "The state has a currency system to circulate goods, benefit the people, and bridge want and plenty; from Qin and Han through Tang and Song, public and private all used coin alike;
translations.idiomatic: In year 18 he memorialized, "The state has a currency system to circulate goods and benefit the people. From Qin and Han through Tang and Song, public and private alike used coin;

sentences.zh: 至金、元，以銀與錢鈔並行；

translations.literal: under Jin and Yuan, silver circulated together with coin and paper notes;
translations.idiomatic: under Jin and Yuan, silver circulated together with coin and paper notes;

sentences.zh: 至明中葉，乃專資於銀。

translations.literal: by mid-Ming the state relied chiefly on silver.
translations.idiomatic: by mid-Ming the state relied chiefly on silver.

sentences.zh: 闖逆之亂，或沉江河，或埋山谷，又以貪吏厚藏，銀益少，民益困。

translations.literal: In the turmoil of the rebel Li, some was sunk in rivers or buried in valleys, and corrupt officials hoarded heavily, so silver grew scarcer and the people grew more distressed.
translations.idiomatic: In the turmoil of the rebel Li, silver was sunk in rivers or buried in mountains, and corrupt officials hoarded heavily, so silver grew scarcer and the people more distressed.

sentences.zh: 今欲救天下之窮，惟有多鑄錢。

translations.literal: To rescue the empire's poverty today, nothing but casting more coin will suffice.
translations.idiomatic: To rescue the empire from poverty today, nothing but casting more coin will suffice.

sentences.zh: 鑄錢所資，銅六鉛四，而可采之山，所司每深諱之，蓋恐時有時無，貽累償稅。

translations.literal: Coin casting requires six parts copper and four lead; yet the offices in charge of each mineable mountain usually conceal this deeply, fearing supply may be intermittent and leave them liable for compensating taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Coin requires six parts copper and four lead, yet officials in charge of mineable mountains usually conceal production, fearing intermittent supply will leave them liable for compensating taxes.

sentences.zh: 且上官聞其地開採，此挾彼制，誅求甚多也。

translations.literal: Moreover, when superiors hear that a place is being opened for mining, they use this to control others and exact much.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when superiors hear that a place is being mined, they use it to control subordinates and exact much.

sentences.zh: 臣謂宜令天下產銅鉛之地，任民採取，有則以十分二輸稅於官，無則聽之州縣自行稽察，毋使多官旁撓。

translations.literal: I say that wherever copper and lead are produced under Heaven, the people should be allowed to gather them; when there is production, two-tenths should be paid in tax to the government, and when there is none the prefectures and counties should inspect on their own, without many officials interfering on the side.
translations.idiomatic: I say that wherever copper and lead are found, the people should be allowed to gather them, paying two-tenths in tax to the government when there is output, while prefectures and counties inspect on their own without many officials interfering.

sentences.zh: 報採多者予議敘，則官與民皆樂為，資以鼓鑄，錢不可勝用矣。」

translations.literal: Those who report much production should receive consideration for promotion, then officials and people alike will be glad to act, resources will supply casting, and coin will be more than enough for use."
translations.idiomatic: Those who report high output should be considered for promotion; then officials and people alike will be glad to act, supplies will feed the mints, and coin will be more than enough."

sentences.zh: 下九卿詳議，擬例以上，得旨：「採銅關係國計，其令各督撫率屬殫力奉行。」

translations.literal: The memorial was referred to the Nine Ministers for detailed deliberation; regulations were drafted and submitted, and an imperial rescript said: "Copper mining bears on state finance; let each governor-general lead subordinates to carry it out with full effort."
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the Nine Ministers; regulations were drafted and submitted, and the emperor ordered, "Copper mining bears on state finance; let every governor-general lead subordinates to carry it out with full effort."

sentences.zh: 六善以老病乞罷，上不許。

translations.literal: Liushan begged to retire on grounds of age and illness; the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Liushan begged to retire on grounds of age and illness, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 二十年，命致仕。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was ordered to retire.
translations.idiomatic: In year 20 he was ordered to retire.

sentences.zh: 三十年，卒於家，年七十一。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he died at home, aged seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: In year 30 he died at home, aged seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 杜臻，字肇餘，浙江秀水人。

translations.literal: Du Zhen, courtesy name Zhaoyu, was a native of Xiushui in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zhen, whose courtesy name was Zhaoyu, came from Xiushui in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 順治十五年進士，改庶吉士，散館，授編修。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the fifteenth year of Shunzhi, he became a Hanlin bachelor, and after leaving the academy was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: A Shunzhi year 15 jinshi, he became a Hanlin bachelor and, after leaving the academy, was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 累遷內閣學士，擢吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He rose in succession to Academician of the Grand Secretariat and was promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Academician of the Grand Secretariat and was promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 國初以海上多事，下令遷東南各省沿海居民於內地，畫界而設之禁。

translations.literal: Early in the dynasty, because affairs at sea were numerous, an order moved coastal residents of the southeastern provinces inland and drew a boundary to set prohibitions.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the dynasty, because of troubles at sea, an order moved coastal residents of the southeastern provinces inland and drew a boundary to enforce prohibitions.

sentences.zh: 界外皆棄地，流民無所歸，去為盜。

translations.literal: Land beyond the boundary was abandoned, and displaced people had nowhere to go and turned to banditry.
translations.idiomatic: Land beyond the boundary was abandoned, and displaced people with nowhere to go turned to banditry.

sentences.zh: 及師定金門、廈門，總督姚啟聖請以界外地按籍還民，弛海禁，收魚鹽之利給軍食，廷臣持不可。

translations.literal: When the armies pacified Kinmen and Xiamen, Governor Yao Qisheng asked that land beyond the boundary be returned to the people by household register, that maritime prohibitions be relaxed, and that profits from fish and salt supply military food; court ministers held this impossible.
translations.idiomatic: When Kinmen and Xiamen were pacified, Governor-General Yao Qisheng asked that land beyond the boundary be returned by household register, maritime prohibitions relaxed, and profits from fish and salt used for military supplies; court ministers opposed it.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十二年，台灣平，上命以界外地還民。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Kangxi Taiwan was pacified and the emperor ordered land beyond the boundary returned to the people.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi year 22 Taiwan was pacified and the emperor ordered land beyond the boundary returned to the people.

sentences.zh: 會給事中傅感丁請以江、浙、閩、粵濱海界外地招徠開墾，乃命臻及內閣學士席柱赴福建、廣東察視展界，進臻工部尚書。

translations.literal: At the same time Supervising Censor Fu Ganding asked that coastal land beyond the boundary in Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, and Guangdong be recruited for reclamation; the court then ordered Zhen and Academician Xizhu to go to Fujian and Guangdong to inspect boundary extension, and Zhen was promoted to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Supervising Censor Fu Ganding asked that coastal land beyond the boundary in Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, and Guangdong be opened for reclamation. The court ordered Zhen and Academician Xizhu to Fujian and Guangdong to inspect boundary extension, and Zhen was promoted to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 臻與席柱如廣東，自欽州防城始，遵海以東而北，歷府七、州三、縣二十九、衛六、所十七、巡檢司十六、台城堡砦二十一，還民地二萬八千一百九十二頃，復業丁口三萬一千三百。
